requirements.title: The application footer shall display the application name and semantic version in the format "Summit vX.Y.Z", sourced from package.json#version

vision.paraphrase: The tool-hygiene baseline declares the footer as the user-visible version surface, fed from package.json so users always know what they are running.

conops.paraphrase: First boot shows the footer version, establishing transparency from the very first visit.

requirements.title: The application shall emit a startup log line containing its name and semantic version at INFO level as the first console record on boot

vision.paraphrase: Startup version stamping is the declared browser-side analog of process-startup log stamping.

conops.paraphrase: Boot prints the version line before anything else happens, so diagnostics start from a known point.

requirements.title: The application shall define its semantic version in exactly one source, package.json#version, such that a change there changes both the footer and the startup log line

vision.paraphrase: Version has a single source of truth by declaration; every display point must derive from it.

conops.paraphrase: The footer a returning user sees must always agree with what the app reports about itself at boot.

requirements.title: The application logger shall emit records at the DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR levels in human-readable plain-text format "[LEVEL] message" via the corresponding console methods

vision.paraphrase: The logging convention fixes the four levels and the [LEVEL] message plain-text format through console methods.

conops.paraphrase: All diagnostic output across the operational scenarios flows through this one console convention.

requirements.title: The application shall display user-facing error messages in the page that name the problem AND the next user action, never console-only

vision.paraphrase: The error-message standard requires problem plus next action, rendered in the UI.
Inline errors that name the problem and the next action are a stated design principle.

conops.paraphrase: Every failure a user can trigger (bad input, unreadable data) must be recoverable from the page alone.

requirements.title: The application shall boot directly into a usable single-screen interface with no account, configuration, or setup step

vision.paraphrase: Goal G6: opens to a usable app with no account and no configuration.

conops.paraphrase: A first-time visitor lands on the complete single screen — input, filter, list, footer — ready to act.

requirements.title: The application shall make zero network requests and remain fully functional offline after first load

vision.paraphrase: No network I/O at any point; the app is fully functional offline after first load.
Goal G5: zero network calls, works fully offline.

conops.paraphrase: The returning user opens Summit with no network and everything still works.

coverage_gaps.note: G7 is about the repo's docs and git history teaching the peak-workflow lifecycle — satisfied by the repository itself, not by observable app behavior, so it is intentionally not a TOR.
